Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer said about it: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.
Enclosure and Structural Designer said about it: I take up the infiltration method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) that Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer used, Manager.
Manager said about it: Array need 3.52 kilowatt peak in the required peak estimate (E82) is met by 3.60 kilowatt peak in that same grown-array yield calc (E83), split layout in the split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels, door method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 millimetre door in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) supports eight-opening discipline, and full-tonne heat 25.0 kilowatt-hour in the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per batch in that revised steady-load simulation (E28) leaves the 43 degree pull-down as named bench test, not a block.
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer said about it: I take up the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) you put on the board, which states 900 millimetre doors with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains and self-closing hinges, which from refrigeration means 4 air changes per day cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, by the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), so 8 openings discipline holds.

statements.text: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.
I take up the infiltration method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) that Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer used, Manager.

Array need 3.52 kilowatt peak in the required peak estimate (E82) is met by 3.60 kilowatt peak in that same grown-array yield calc (E83), split layout in the split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels, door method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 millimetre door in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) supports eight-opening discipline, and full-tonne heat 25.0 kilowatt-hour in the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per batch in that revised steady-load simulation (E28) leaves the 43 degree pull-down as named bench test, not a block.

I take up the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) you put on the board, which states 900 millimetre doors with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains and self-closing hinges, which from refrigeration means 4 air changes per day cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, by the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), so 8 openings discipline holds.
